newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil up, looks to China.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil up, looks to China.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps rose late afternoon on Wednesday in active trade on expectations of buying from China and news of the shutdown of a thermal cracking unit in Singapore in August for three weeks, traders said.
"Gas oil is up because people think China is going to come back to the market and Shell is shutting down its cracker," one trader said.
August swaps were last quoted at $22.40/$22.50 per barrel, up 30 cents from Tuesday's $22.10/$22.20 per barrel, brokers said.
August traded earlier in the day at $22.20, $22.25 and $22.33 with trades done for September at $22.90, $22.95 and $23.00, they said.
September was last quoted at $23.10/$23.20, from Tuesday's $22.80/$22.90.
The gas oil swaps market has since early Monday risen by about $1.00.

Traders said the fresh buying interest was partly due to expectations of new demand from China which has since April more than halved its monthly purchases to average at about 400,000 tonnes from about 800,000 tonnes.
Diesel stocks in China are easing as a result of the crackdown on smuggling which has forced endusers to buy from local refiners instead of resorting to the cheaper illicit product.
As a result domestic prices of diesel are increasing with some traders say prices have risen by about $20 per tonne, from around $210-$230.
Earlier Wednesday, Shell Singapore said it will shutdown its 82,000-barrel-per-day thermal gas oil unit for a 21-day maintenance in early August.
In the physical market on Tuesday, a buyer emerged for a cargo that was offered at $21.50 per barrel free-on-board Singapore basis but no deal was concluded due to operational differences.
The buying level was 30 cents above Monday's highest traded price.
On Monday, four deals totalling 670,000 barrels were done between $20.90 and $21.20 per barrel on a free-on-board Singapore basis.

The fuel oil market edged up slightly on sutained buying support from a local trader with August last quoted up 25 cents at $98.75/$99.50, brokers said. August traded earlier in the day at $99.00, they said.
